profile.headline: Research systems builder · Founder, QNFO: open, auditable AI-assisted research · 15 years of national data and policy research (FHWA, AARP Livability Index)

about:
I build the machinery that turns messy evidence into decisions people can trust.

At the U.S. Federal Highway Administration I managed a $1.5M federal research portfolio as a certified Contracting Officer's Representative and helped build the national long-distance travel forecasting model. At AARP's Public Policy Institute I led the Livability Index, which scores U.S. neighborhoods from 50+ data sources across 7 domains.

I now run QNFO, an independent research imprint where an AI-assisted pipeline drafts, referees, revises and corrects papers, and every claim states its status. My current question is what a correct computation really costs in energy (the JPCUB benchmark).

Open to research management, applied AI and research-integrity roles. Earlier work is published under Brad Gudzinas.

experience.title: Founder
experience.description:
Built and run an autonomous research system on Cloudflare that drafts, referees, revises, versions, publishes and corrects papers, with a public errata trail.

Designed the audit method (The Universal Ignorance Audit; Epistemic Legibility in AI-Assisted Science).

Proposed JPCUB, a whole-system energy benchmark for computing (joules per correct answer): measurement protocol, estimates for 17 quantum platforms, and an extension to LLM inference.
